title: Steady work, quitting for studio work, and talk of Lionel Reason
summary: Howard says he has worked constantly except when he left the road for the studios in the 1940s, and the group drifts to Oliver's 1937 pianist.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: In other words, once you became a professional you were working all the time, huh?

Yeah. I mean you were always in demand, huh? I've been very fortunate. I've been working practically all my, ever since I started. Other than the time I quit. Yeah. Which was in the 40s. Yeah. And I didn't quit because, well, I quit to stay in that studio.

Yeah, I quit playing music on pictures. I didn't want to go on the road, see. What kind of music was Joe's band playing? Who's? Oliver's band playing in 37 when you saw it. Oh I didn't hear them. Oh that? I'll tell you who was with them. The piano player, Lionel Reason?

Yes. He was with them then in 37. Oh yeah? We were talking about it. You know when he was working about, oh he played there for a while with us, up until we went on a vacation. I mean he played the relief piano, like Joe Sullivan still. Oh, at Dango? Uh huh. Yeah he played with us for four years. We had a good little while. Didn't he play with Scopey Dango or anything? Uh huh. No. Or with Orie. Or with Orie. Yeah but Orie. I think it's better.
